3

The PDF viewer (pdfviewer.html) displays PDF files: page navigation, zoom, rotation, search, outline and page thumbnails, links, filling in forms, annotations (highlight, text, drawing), printing and password-protected files.

Opening and saving

  • Open (Ctrl+O) opens a PDF file; you can also drop a file onto the window.
  • Password-protected files ask for the password.
  • Save (Ctrl+S) saves the PDF with filled-in form fields and your annotations: directly into the opened file in Chrome/Edge on the desktop, as a download in Firefox and on Android (replace the original file with it). Ctrl+Shift+S saves under a new name.

Navigating

  • ‹ and › go to the previous and next page; type a page number into the page field.
  • ☰ shows the sidebar: Pages shows thumbnails (click one to go to the page), Outline shows the table of contents of the document, if it has one.
  • Links in the document work: internal links jump to the target page.

Zoom and rotation

− and + zoom out and in. The zoom list offers Automatic, Whole page, Page width and fixed sizes. ⟳ rotates all pages by 90 degrees (only the view; the file is not changed).

Search

🔍 or Ctrl+F opens the search bar. The viewer highlights all matches and shows "1 of 3 matches". Next and Previous move between the matches; Match case distinguishes upper and lower case.

Forms and annotations

Form fields can be filled in directly. The Annotate list switches the mode:

Mode Function
Select / fill in forms normal mode: select text, click links, fill in forms
Highlight select text to highlight it
Text click on the page to add a text box
Draw draw with the mouse, pen or finger

Save the file to keep form entries and annotations.

Signing

✍ opens a signature field: draw your signature with the mouse, a pen or a finger, or type your name. Place closes the field; then click or tap the spot on the page where the signature should go (Esc or ✍ cancels). The signature is added to the page as an image (about 6 cm wide) and can be undone like a page operation (📄 → Undo). Save the file to keep it.

This is a visible signature, like one on paper. It is not a digital (cryptographic) signature.

Pages: rearrange, rotate, delete, extract, merge

Tick pages in the thumbnails (☰ → Pages); without ticks the current page is meant. 📄 Pages then offers:

Entry Function
Rotate left / right turns the pages permanently (unlike ⟳, which only turns the view)
Move earlier / later / to position… moves the pages as a block
Delete removes the pages (one page always stays)
Extract as new PDF… saves copies of the pages as a new file; the open file stays unchanged
Insert PDF after… / Append PDF… inserts all pages of one or more other PDF files after the selection or at the end (merging)
Select all pages, Clear selection
Undo undoes the last page operation (also Ctrl+Z)

Save the file to keep the changes. Password-protected PDFs can be read and filled in, but their pages cannot be changed. Form fields, bookmarks and metadata are kept; bookmarks to deleted pages lead nowhere.

Digital signatures

When a PDF contains digital signatures, a line above the page shows the result of the check: ✅ signed by … – the signature is valid, ⚠️ the document was changed after signing (bytes were added after the signature, e.g. filled-in form fields or further signatures – the signed version itself is intact) or ❌ the signature is NOT valid (the signed content was changed, or the signature does not belong to the certificate). A click on the line, or ✍ in the sidebar, shows every signature with signer, date, reason, location, the certificate (issuer, validity, self-signed or expired) and the certificate chain included in the signature.

The check is done in the browser (RSA and ECDSA signatures, SHA-1 to SHA-512). Whether a certificate is trustworthy is not decided: offline there is no store of trusted root certificates, so a valid signature only proves that the content has not changed since it was signed with that certificate. Compare the certificate with the signer if in doubt.

Printing

🖨 prepares all pages and opens the print dialog of the browser. Form entries and annotations are printed as well.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

Files

Keys Function
Ctrl+O Open
Ctrl+S Save
Ctrl+Shift+S Save as

Editing

Keys Function
Ctrl+F Find
Ctrl+Z Undo the last page operation

Help

Keys Function
F1 / ? show this list (outside of text fields)

On phones and tablets

The toolbar can be scrolled sideways, the sidebar (☰) opens over the pages and closes when you choose a page or chapter (or tap next to it). Use the zoom buttons or the zoom list for the page size.
